20	
21	| # | Risque | P / I | Parade |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| 1 | Format non contractuel (nouveaux types, champs renommés) | haute / haute | Décoder ligne à ligne dans une struct qui ne porte **que** des champs numériques et des identifiants, ignorer les types inconnus, compteurs `skipped` et `unknownVersion` affichés dans l'en-tête (dégradation visible). Fixtures datées et versionnées. |
24	| 2 | Dédup | certaine / haute | Clé `message.id` (+ `requestId`), la dernière ligne gagne, carte par session (et non par fichier) : elle couvre un futur parent qui recopierait les lignes des sous-agents. Exclure `<synthetic>`. Fixer en S-01 la référence (ccusage ou `cost-state`) : si ccusage garde la première ligne, l'écart de 2,7 % est structurel. |
25	| 3 | Lecture incrémentale | moyenne / haute | Un offset par fichier ; une dernière ligne sans `\n` est gardée en reste et relue au tick suivant ; une taille inférieure à l'offset déclenche une relecture complète ; une ligne au-delà du plafond est sautée et comptée. On suppose les fichiers en ajout seul (les `compact_boundary` sont ajoutées, pas réécrites). |
26	| 4 | Polling ou watcher | moyenne / moyenne | **Polling `tea.Tick` (2 s) + `stat`**, le modèle existant (suivi du viewer, ports, conteneurs). Pas de `fsnotify` : c'est une nouvelle dépendance, peu fiable sur les montages 9p, virtiofs et WSL, précisément ceux de S-08. Ne sonder que la session ouverte et le répertoire `subagents/` (nouveaux agents). Arrêt quand la session est inactive et que tous les `finished` sont à vrai. |
27	| 5 | Règle 110 / `Update` non bloquant | faible si conçu ainsi / haute | Le `Cmd` reçoit une **copie** des offsets et rend `UsageDeltaMsg{gen, file, from, to, records}`. `Update` n'applique le delta que si `from == offset courant` et `gen` est le dernier, sinon il l'abandonne (même schéma que `toolsGen`). Une seule lecture en vol par session. `mise run test-race` est obligatoire. |
28	| 6 | Confidentialité | moyenne / haute | Les lignes contiennent prompts, thinking, `wireToolInputs`, `toolUseResult.prompt`. On ne loggue jamais une ligne, et une erreur de décodage ne cite que le fichier et l'offset. On ne compte les blocs `tool_use` que par leur `type`. `description` et `ai-title` ne s'affichent pas (voir Q3). |
29	| 7 | Intégration au routeur | faible / moyenne | Les tests de contrat attrapent les oublis (`TestEveryViewSuppliesItsHeaderAndHelp`, keymap, `AllViewNames`). Points d'entrée listés en §3. |
30	| 8 | Entrée non fiable (S-08) | moyenne / moyenne | Un sandbox écrit ces fichiers : plafond de ligne, pas de suivi des liens symboliques hors des racines, pas de décodage de chemin depuis le nom de répertoire (lire `cwd`). |
31	| 9 | Portabilité | faible / moyenne | `~/.claude` vient de `os.UserHomeDir`, et `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` est honoré s'il est défini (Windows inclus). |
32	
33	## 2. Effort par story
34	
35	| Story | Effort | Hypothèse qui le justifie |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| S-01 spike | **S** (½ à 1 j) | Ce document en a fait une partie (structure, dédup, `meta.json`). Reste à faire : lancer ccusage sur 3 sessions et noter sa règle de dédup, vérifier `sbx` **sur l'hôte qui le lance**, créer la fixture synthétique « autre version ». |
38	| S-02 parseur | **M** | Package pur sans TUI ; struct à champs numériques ; dédup ; tolérance ; 5 à 8 fixtures. Le critère des 2 % dépend de la référence choisie en S-01. |
39	| S-03 liste + arbre | **M**, découpage conseillé | C'est la première vue : enregistrement complet (§3). **S-03a** liste des sessions (projet = `cwd`, date = mtime, triées) : S. **S-03b** `→` vers la table des agents (orchestrateur puis sous-agents, rôle, modèle, tokens) sur le modèle runs → targets de `:jobs` : S. |
40	| S-04 tri + part | **S** | `.` et `Less` sont fournis par `datatable`. Colonne `%` en `SizingFixed` ; le dernier arrondi est absorbé par la ligne principale pour que la somme fasse 100. Distinguer deux agents du même rôle se fait par l'`agentId` court. |
41	| S-05 direct | **L**, à redécouper | **S-05a** lecteur incrémental dans le package (offsets, reste de ligne, troncature, plafond), sans TUI : M. **S-05b** polling dans la vue (tick, `gen`, découverte des nouveaux agents, arrêt sur session terminée, `ctrl+r` = relecture complète) : M. |
42	| S-06 état / activité | **M** | État = `finished`, sinon « en cours » si la session est vivante, sinon « inconnu ». Inactif = aucune ligne depuis plus de 5 min. Compter les `tool_use` par `(message.id, apiBlockIndex)`, car les lignes streamées répètent le message. Durée = premier → dernier `timestamp`. |
43	| S-07 coût indicatif | **M** | Nouvelle section de configuration (`agent_usage.prices` par modèle, avec les tarifs distincts cache 5 min / 1 h / lecture), `-` si le tarif est inconnu. C'est une carte, pas un scalaire : la vue `:cfg` ne l'édite pas, l'édition passe par le YAML (Q4). |
44	| S-08 sandbox | **S** (option A) à **L** (option B) | Avec l'option A, DevDesk n'ajoute que des racines de transcripts multiples et une colonne « Source » ; le reste est une procédure `sbx` documentée. À réécrire après S-01. |
45	
46	## 3. Packages et intégration
47	
48	- `internal/agentusage` (pur, sans Bubble Tea) : `Discover(roots) []SessionRef`, `type Reader` (offsets et reste, valeur copiable), `ReadDelta(ref, offsets) (Delta, error)`, `type Aggregate` avec `Apply(Delta) Aggregate` (dédup, totaux par agent), `Liveness(ref)` (`sessions/*.json` + mtime). `internal/agentusage/pricing` arrivera avec S-07.
49	- `internal/ui/agentusage` : `Model` (deux niveaux `datatable`, fil d'Ariane sous la table, Règle 123), `availability.go` (Règle 130), `GetHelpContent` (Règle 114), les 4 méthodes de `HeaderView` (compteur de sessions et d'agents dans `GetHeaderInfo`), et l'état de chargement dans le pied de page (Règles 128 et 139).
50	- Points d'entrée : `internal/command/parser.go` (`ViewAgentUsage`, table `viewNames`), `internal/app/command_line.go` (`createView`), `docs/architecture/` (nouveau fichier, et une ligne dans le tableau de `.claude/CLAUDE.md`).
51	- **Commande** : `:usage` / `:us` (Hypothèse : `ag`, `us` et `u` sont libres, à arbitrer en Q1).
52	- **Clavier : aucune lettre d'action en MVP.** `→`/`enter` descend, `←`/`esc` remonte, `.` trie, `/` filtre, `ctrl+r` relit. Les lettres libres (`Q`, `Z`) ne sont pas consommées. Un éventuel filtre « actives seulement » serait une minuscule déclarée dans `keymap.localToggles`. Plus tard : `Y` (copier l'id de session), déjà dans le vocabulaire.
53	- Pas de `jobs.Run` : le polling n'est pas un travail lancé par l'utilisateur. On ne l'inscrit au registre que si l'on veut voir la relecture complète dans `:jobs`, ce qui n'est pas nécessaire.
54	
55	## 4. Sandbox `sbx` : transport
56	
57	D'après des sources tierces, les transcripts d'un `sbx` vivent dans un **volume géré par le kit** et ne sont pas sur l'hôte ; `sbx create` accepte des montages supplémentaires ([sbx/claude-mixin](https://hub.docker.com/r/sbx/claude-mixin), [DEV Community](https://dev.to/thr0n/claude-code-in-docker-sandboxes-239g)). Non vérifié : `sbx` est absent de cette machine.
58	
59	| Option | Avantages | Risques |
60	|---|---|---|
61	| **A. Monter un répertoire hôte dédié** (`~/.devdesk/agent-usage/sbx/<nom>`) comme `~/.claude/projects` du sandbox ; DevDesk le déclare comme racine supplémentaire | Aucun code de transport ; même parseur ; quasi temps réel ; survit à la suppression du sandbox | Il faut recréer le sandbox (`sbx create`) ; le sandbox écrit sur l'hôte. **Ne jamais monter tout `~/.claude`** : le sandbox pourrait écrire `settings.json`/hooks exécutés par l'hôte (évasion). Montages 9p/virtiofs : d'où le polling. |
62	| B. Lire le volume via `sbx exec … tail -c +offset` | Rien à reconfigurer côté sandbox | CLI expérimentale, un processus par tick, latence, dépend de l'auth `sbx` ; effort L |
63	| C. Hook dans le sandbox (`Stop`, `SubagentStop`) qui copie le transcript dans le dépôt monté (`.worktrees/…`) | Utilise le montage existant | Les hooks ne portent pas de tokens (il faut copier le fichier), écrit dans l'arbre du dépôt (gitignore), installe une config dans chaque sandbox, latence par événement |
64	| D. OTel : le sandbox exporte en OTLP vers un récepteur DevDesk | Attribution officielle (`agent_id` sur les événements) | Hors MVP (brief), récepteur à embarquer, sortie réseau du sandbox vers l'hôte via le proxy `sbx`, 5 s/60 s, variables d'environnement par session |
65	
66	**Recommandation : A**, avec un montage **dédié et limité aux transcripts**, sous réserve que S-01 confirme sur l'hôte `sbx` que (a) le montage peut remplacer `~/.claude/projects` sans casser `claude -c`, et (b) les fichiers sont visibles et ajoutés au fil de l'eau côté hôte. Sinon, se replier sur C.
67	
68	## 5. Ordre de livraison
69	
70	1. S-01 (Go / no-go, dédup de référence, constat `sbx`).
71	2. S-02 puis S-05a (même package, en TDD, sans TUI ; parallélisable une fois l'API `Delta`/`Aggregate` figée).
72	3. S-03a, puis S-03b et S-04 (S-04 parallélisable avec S-03b).
73	4. S-05b (critère de succès « en direct < 3 s »).
74	5. S-06, puis S-07 (indépendante, peut glisser), puis S-08 selon S-01.
75	
76	## Questions ouvertes (pour l'utilisateur)
77	
78	1. **Nom de la commande** : `:usage`/`:us` (recommandé), `:agents`/`:ag`, ou `:agent-usage`/`:au` ?
79	2. **Référence des 2 %** : ccusage (externe, règle de dédup à vérifier) ou les lignes `cost-state` de Claude Code (interne, par modèle et non par agent) ? Recommandation : `cost-state` pour le total de session, ccusage en contrôle secondaire.
80	3. **Afficher `meta.description` / `ai-title`** pour distinguer les agents et nommer les sessions ? Ce sont des textes de tâche, contraires à « jamais de contenu ». Recommandation : non en MVP (agent = rôle + `agentId` court, session = projet + date).
81	4. **Tarifs (S-07)** : édition YAML seule acceptable, ou faut-il un éditeur dans `:cfg` (ce qui ajoute M) ?
82	5. **Où tourne `sbx`** : sur l'hôte Windows évoqué dans `.claude/CLAUDE.md` ? DevDesk lit-il alors des chemins Windows (`%USERPROFILE%\.claude`) ? Cela conditionne S-01 et S-08.
83	6. **Recréer les sandboxes** avec un montage supplémentaire (option A) : acceptable ?
84

| 8 | Entrée non fiable (S-08) | moyenne / moyenne | Un sandbox écrit ces fichiers : plafond de ligne, pas de suivi des liens symboliques hors des racines, pas de décodage de chemin depuis le nom de répertoire (lire `cwd`). |
| 9 | Portabilité | faible / moyenne | `~/.claude` vient de `os.UserHomeDir`, et `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` est honoré s'il est défini (Windows inclus). |

## 2. Effort par story

| Story | Effort | Hypothèse qui le justifie |
|---|---|---|
| S-01 spike | **S** (½ à 1 j) | Ce document en a fait une partie (structure, dédup, `meta.json`). Reste à faire : lancer ccusage sur 3 sessions et noter sa règle de dédup, vérifier `sbx` **sur l'hôte qui le lance**, créer la fixture synthétique « autre version ». |
| S-02 parseur | **M** | Package pur sans TUI ; struct à champs numériques ; dédup ; tolérance ; 5 à 8 fixtures. Le critère des 2 % dépend de la référence choisie en S-01. |
| S-03 liste + arbre | **M**, découpage conseillé | C'est la première vue : enregistrement complet (§3). **S-03a** liste des sessions (projet = `cwd`, date = mtime, triées) : S. **S-03b** `→` vers la table des agents (orchestrateur puis sous-agents, rôle, modèle, tokens) sur le modèle runs → targets de `:jobs` : S. |
| S-04 tri + part | **S** | `.` et `Less` sont fournis par `datatable`. Colonne `%` en `SizingFixed` ; le dernier arrondi est absorbé par la ligne principale pour que la somme fasse 100. Distinguer deux agents du même rôle se fait par l'`agentId` court. |
| S-05 direct | **L**, à redécouper | **S-05a** lecteur incrémental dans le package (offsets, reste de ligne, troncature, plafond), sans TUI : M. **S-05b** polling dans la vue (tick, `gen`, découverte des nouveaux agents, arrêt sur session terminée, `ctrl+r` = relecture complète) : M. |
| S-06 état / activité | **M** | État = `finished`, sinon « en cours » si la session est vivante, sinon « inconnu ». Inactif = aucune ligne depuis plus de 5 min. Compter les `tool_use` par `(message.id, apiBlockIndex)`, car les lignes streamées répètent le message. Durée = premier → dernier `timestamp`. |
| S-07 coût indicatif | **M** | Nouvelle section de configuration (`agent_usage.prices` par modèle, avec les tarifs distincts cache 5 min / 1 h / lecture), `-` si le tarif est inconnu. C'est une carte, pas un scalaire : la vue `:cfg` ne l'édite pas, l'édition passe par le YAML (Q4). |
| S-08 sandbox | **S** (option A) à **L** (option B) | Avec l'option A, DevDesk n'ajoute que des racines de transcripts multiples et une colonne « Source » ; le reste est une procédure `sbx` documentée. À réécrire après S-01. |

## 3. Packages et intégration

- `internal/agentusage` (pur, sans Bubble Tea) : `Discover(roots) []SessionRef`, `type Reader` (offsets et reste, valeur copiable), `ReadDelta(ref, offsets) (Delta, error)`, `type Aggregate` avec `Apply(Delta) Aggregate` (dédup, totaux par agent), `Liveness(ref)` (`sessions/*.json` + mtime). `internal/agentusage/pricing` arrivera avec S-07.
- `internal/ui/agentusage` : `Model` (deux niveaux `datatable`, fil d'Ariane sous la table, Règle 123), `availability.go` (Règle 130), `GetHelpContent` (Règle 114), les 4 méthodes de `HeaderView` (compteur de sessions et d'agents dans `GetHeaderInfo`), et l'état de chargement dans le pied de page (Règles 128 et 139).
- Points d'entrée : `internal/command/parser.go` (`ViewAgentUsage`, table `viewNames`), `internal/app/command_line.go` (`createView`), `docs/architecture/` (nouveau fichier, et une ligne dans le tableau de `.claude/CLAUDE.md`).
- **Commande** : `:usage` / `:us` (Hypothèse : `ag`, `us` et `u` sont libres, à arbitrer en Q1).
- **Clavier : aucune lettre d'action en MVP.** `→`/`enter` descend, `←`/`esc` remonte, `.` trie, `/` filtre, `ctrl+r` relit. Les lettres libres (`Q`, `Z`) ne sont pas consommées. Un éventuel filtre « actives seulement » serait une minuscule déclarée dans `keymap.localToggles`. Plus tard : `Y` (copier l'id de session), déjà dans le vocabulaire.
- Pas de `jobs.Run` : le polling n'est pas un travail lancé par l'utilisateur. On ne l'inscrit au registre que si l'on veut voir la relecture complète dans `:jobs`, ce qui n'est pas nécessaire.

## 4. Sandbox `sbx` : transport

D'après des sources tierces, les transcripts d'un `sbx` vivent dans un **volume géré par le kit** et ne sont pas sur l'hôte ; `sbx create` accepte des montages supplémentaires ([sbx/claude-mixin](https://hub.docker.com/r/sbx/claude-mixin), [DEV Community](https://dev.to/thr0n/claude-code-in-docker-sandboxes-239g)). Non vérifié : `sbx` est absent de cette machine.

| Option | Avantages | Risques |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Monter un répertoire hôte dédié** (`~/.devdesk/agent-usage/sbx/<nom>`) comme `~/.claude/projects` du sandbox ; DevDesk le déclare comme racine supplémentaire | Aucun code de transport ; même parseur ; quasi temps réel ; survit à la suppression du sandbox | Il faut recréer le sandbox (`sbx create`) ; le sandbox écrit sur l'hôte. **Ne jamais monter tout `~/.claude`** : le sandbox pourrait écrire `settings.json`/hooks exécutés par l'hôte (évasion). Montages 9p/virtiofs : d'où le polling. |
| B. Lire le volume via `sbx exec … tail -c +offset` | Rien à reconfigurer côté sandbox | CLI expérimentale, un processus par tick, latence, dépend de l'auth `sbx` ; effort L |
| C. Hook dans le sandbox (`Stop`, `SubagentStop`) qui copie le transcript dans le dépôt monté (`.worktrees/…`) | Utilise le montage existant | Les hooks ne portent pas de tokens (il faut copier le fichier), écrit dans l'arbre du dépôt (gitignore), installe une config dans chaque sandbox, latence par événement |
| D. OTel : le sandbox exporte en OTLP vers un récepteur DevDesk | Attribution officielle (`agent_id` sur les événements) | Hors MVP (brief), récepteur à embarquer, sortie réseau du sandbox vers l'hôte via le proxy `sbx`, 5 s/60 s, variables d'environnement par session |

**Recommandation : A**, avec un montage **dédié et limité aux transcripts**, sous réserve que S-01 confirme sur l'hôte `sbx` que (a) le montage peut remplacer `~/.claude/projects` sans casser `claude -c`, et (b) les fichiers sont visibles et ajoutés au fil de l'eau côté hôte. Sinon, se replier sur C.

## 5. Ordre de livraison

1. S-01 (Go / no-go, dédup de référence, constat `sbx`).
2. S-02 puis S-05a (même package, en TDD, sans TUI ; parallélisable une fois l'API `Delta`/`Aggregate` figée).
3. S-03a, puis S-03b et S-04 (S-04 parallélisable avec S-03b).
4. S-05b (critère de succès « en direct < 3 s »).
5. S-06, puis S-07 (indépendante, peut glisser), puis S-08 selon S-01.

## Questions ouvertes (pour l'utilisateur)

1. **Nom de la commande** : `:usage`/`:us` (recommandé), `:agents`/`:ag`, ou `:agent-usage`/`:au` ?
2. **Référence des 2 %** : ccusage (externe, règle de dédup à vérifier) ou les lignes `cost-state` de Claude Code (interne, par modèle et non par agent) ? Recommandation : `cost-state` pour le total de session, ccusage en contrôle secondaire.
3. **Afficher `meta.description` / `ai-title`** pour distinguer les agents et nommer les sessions ? Ce sont des textes de tâche, contraires à « jamais de contenu ». Recommandation : non en MVP (agent = rôle + `agentId` court, session = projet + date).
4. **Tarifs (S-07)** : édition YAML seule acceptable, ou faut-il un éditeur dans `:cfg` (ce qui ajoute M) ?
5. **Où tourne `sbx`** : sur l'hôte Windows évoqué dans `.claude/CLAUDE.md` ? DevDesk lit-il alors des chemins Windows (`%USERPROFILE%\.claude`) ? Cela conditionne S-01 et S-08.
6. **Recréer les sandboxes** avec un montage supplémentaire (option A) : acceptable ?

1	# Agent usage — `internal/agentusage`
2	
3	> DevDesk architecture notes. Referenced from `.claude/CLAUDE.md`;
4	> read this file when working on the code it describes.
5	
6	Two pieces: the data layer `internal/agentusage` (sections up to
7	"Verification") and the `:agent-usage` view `internal/ui/agentusageview`
8	(last section, DEVDESK-41).
9	
10	## What the package is for
11	
12	`internal/agentusage` reads the transcripts Claude Code writes under its
13	projects directory and returns, for one session, the **token counts per
14	agent** (the orchestrator and each sub-agent). It is the data layer of the
15	agent usage monitor (DEVDESK-40, spike S-01 then step S-02).
16	
17	What it does **not** do:
18	
19	- no cost, price or quota computation;
20	- no storage, no cache, nothing written to disk;
21	- no UI, no Bubble Tea import (the view lives in `internal/ui/agentusageview`);
22	- no dependency beyond the Go standard library.
23	
24	**The public API is a contract.** Every exported symbol in the table below
25	(`Tokens`, `Agent`, `State`, `Usage`, `Diagnostics`, `FileIssue`, `IssueKind`,
26	`SessionFiles`, `SubAgentFiles`, `ParseSession`, `LocateSession`, `ProjectsRoot`,
27	`ListSessions`, `Session`, `Listing`)
28	is consumed by S-03b, S-04 and S-05a. Changing a field is a change to those
29	stories; add, do not rename.
30	
31	## Public API
32	
33	| Symbol | Role |
34	|---|---|
35	| `ProjectsRoot()` | `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`, else `~/.claude/projects` |
36	| `LocateSession(parentTranscript)` | from `<dir>/<uuid>.jsonl`, finds `<dir>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` and their meta files. Returns `SessionFiles{ID, Parent, SubAgents}`. A missing session directory means no sub-agents. Returns an error if the parent is missing, is a symbolic link or is not a regular file. |
37	| `SessionFiles` | `ID`, `Parent` (path of the parent transcript), `SubAgents []SubAgentFiles` |
38	| `SubAgentFiles` | `ID`, `Transcript`, `Meta` (`""` if the meta file is absent) |
39	| `ParseSession(SessionFiles)` | returns `Usage`. Fails only if the parent transcript cannot be opened: a missing file, a symbolic link or a non-regular file is an **error**, not an ignored input. |
40	| `ListSessions(root)` | lists `<root>/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl`, one level deep, never recursively. Returns `Listing`. A missing root is an empty `Listing` and no error; a root that is not a directory or cannot be read is an error naming the base name only. The root itself may be a symbolic link (the user's own choice); anything below it may not. |
41	| `Session{ID, Parent, Project, ModTime}` | `Parent` is a full path, for `LocateSession`, and is never logged. `Project` is the working directory read from the transcript (`cwd`), sanitized and capped at 4096 bytes, or `""` if none. `ModTime` is the transcript's modification time. |
42	| `Listing{Sessions, Omitted}` | `Sessions` newest `ModTime` first, ties by ID ascending. `Omitted` counts what was not listed: linked or non-regular transcripts, linked or unreadable project directories, and sessions past the cap. |
43	| `Tokens{Input, Output, CacheRead, CacheWrite}` | `int64` counters; `Total()` and `Add()` saturate at `math.MaxInt64` |
44	| `Agent` | `ID` (empty for the orchestrator), `Main`, `Type`, `Models`, `Tokens`, `Messages`, `PartialMessages`, `State`, `SpawnDepth`; `PartialOutput()` |
45	| `State` | `StateUnknown`, `StateFinished`, `StateUnfinished` |
46	| `Usage` | `SessionID`, `Agents` (orchestrator first, then sub-agents by ID), `Versions`, `Diagnostics`; `Total()` |
47	| `Diagnostics` | `UnreadableLines`, `OversizedLines`, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, `MetaMissing`, `MetaUnreadable`, `TruncatedFiles`, `Files []FileIssue`; `Degraded()` |
48	| `FileIssue{File, Offset, Kind}` | one skipped line or file problem. `File` is a base name. `Offset` is the byte offset of the line (for `IssueReadError`, the offset consumed; for `IssueOpenFailed`, 0). Entries are sorted by offset within each file. |
49	| `IssueKind` | `IssueUnreadable` (not JSON, truncated, or bad counters), `IssueOversized` (longer than `MaxLineBytes`), `IssueOpenFailed` (a sub-agent transcript could not be opened), `IssueReadError` (reading stopped on an I/O error) |
50	
51	`State` is read from the `finished` key of the sub-agent's meta file: `true`
52	is `StateFinished`, `false` is `StateUnfinished`. An absent, null or
53	wrongly typed key, a missing or unreadable meta file, and the orchestrator
54	are `StateUnknown`.
55	
56	## Transcript format
57	
58	```
59	projects/<project>/<uuid>.jsonl                          orchestrator
60	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl     one per sub-agent
61	projects/<project>/<uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.meta.json agentType, finished, spawnDepth
62	projects/<project>/<uuid>/tool-results/                  never read
63	```
64	
65	Each transcript line is a JSON object. Only `version` and `message.{id, model,
66	stop_reason, usage}` are read; the four counters are `input_tokens`,
67	`output_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens`.
68	Content, tools and descriptions are not declared in the decoding structs, so
69	`encoding/json` skips them without keeping them. Nothing is searched
70	recursively. Symbolic links are handled by position:
71	
72	- a **parent transcript** that is a symbolic link or not a regular file is an
73	  **error** (`LocateSession` and `ParseSession`);
74	- a sub-agent transcript that is a link or not a regular file is not listed by
75	  `LocateSession`; if one is passed to `ParseSession` anyway, it stays in
76	  `Agents` with an `IssueOpenFailed` entry;
77	- a meta file that is a link or not a regular file counts as missing
78	  (`MetaMissing`);
79	- a session directory or `subagents/` directory that is a link means no
80	  sub-agents.
81	
82	## Aggregation rules
83	
84	- **Last line wins per `message.id`**, over the whole session. Streaming writes
85	  the same message several times; only the final state counts.
86	- **A message seen in several files is attributed to the last file read**
87	  (orchestrator first, then sub-agents sorted by ID). Each such overwrite counts
88	  in `Diagnostics.CrossFileDuplicates`.
89	- **A line without `message.id` counts once**, keyed by file and offset, and
90	  increments `NoMessageID`.
91	- **`<synthetic>` is excluded**: locally generated turns are never billed.
92	- **A line with neither id, model nor usage is ignored** (user and tool-result
93	  lines).
94	- **Partial output**: a message whose last line has a null or absent
95	  `stop_reason` is counted in `Agent.PartialMessages`, and `PartialOutput()` is
96	  true. Its output count is a floor. This is computed for every agent; the UI
97	  decides how to show it.
98	- **Saturation**: sums stop at `math.MaxInt64` instead of wrapping.
99	- An incomplete last line (no newline) is not counted and its file is listed in
100	  `Diagnostics.TruncatedFiles`. If it already exceeds the line cap it is dropped
101	  silently.
102	
103	## Tolerance
104	
105	The format is not a documented API, so the parser degrades rather than fails.
106	
107	- Unknown fields are ignored.
108	- A message with an id or model but **no `usage`** (absent, or renamed by a
109	  newer client) is counted in `Diagnostics.NoUsage` and adds nothing. A
110	  sub-agent with no usable meta `finished` is `StateUnknown`.
111	- Metadata of an unexpected type (`model`, `version`, `agentType`,
112	  `spawnDepth`) costs that field only, not the line.
113	- A counter that is negative, fractional or not a number makes the line
114	  unreadable (`UnreadableLines`). An absent or null counter is 0.
115	- A sub-agent that cannot be opened stays in `Agents` with no tokens and an
116	  `IssueOpenFailed` entry. A read error mid-file keeps what was read and adds
117	  `IssueReadError` at the offset consumed.
118	- A missing meta file counts in `MetaMissing`; an unreadable one in
119	  `MetaUnreadable`.
120	
121	## Privacy
122	
123	`ParseSession` returns **numeric aggregates only**. No prompt, answer, tool
124	input, description or path is ever stored in a `Usage`.
125	
126	**Amendment (DEVDESK-41): `cwd` is now read and displayed.** `ListSessions`
127	alone reads it, to tell sessions apart by project. It is the first non-empty
128	string `cwd` found in the first 8 MiB of a transcript (twice `MaxLineBytes`, so
129	one maximal line can be skipped); the scan stops there and nothing else of the
130	transcript is kept. The view shows the **full path**, with the home folder
131	folded to `~`. The path is sanitized and capped, and is **never logged**: the
132	view logs a failed listing, but its error carries a base name only. A `Usage`
133	still carries no path. This replaces the earlier wording that no path was ever
134	read.
135	
136	- Errors carry the base name of a file, never its full path (`baseOnly`), and
137	  fixed messages instead of `encoding/json` errors, which can quote content.
138	- Text that comes from disk goes through `sanitize`: labels (model, version,
139	  agent type, session and agent IDs, file names; `sanitizeLabel`, cut to 128
140	  bytes) and the `cwd` (cut to 4096 bytes). Replaced by `?`: invalid UTF-8
141	  bytes, every control character (C0, DEL and **C1**, so a raw or encoded
142	  0x9B CSI is caught) and every format character (Unicode category **Cf**:
143	  bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks). Text read from disk reaches a
144	  terminal, where an escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override
145	  would reorder what follows.
146	- `FileIssue.File` is a base name, never a path.
147	- The fixtures plant `SENTINEL-DO-NOT-LEAK` in the `content`, `description`,
148	  `cwd` and tool `input` fields of the transcripts and in the `description`
149	  of the `.meta.json` files. Tests check that it never appears in a `Usage` or
150	  an error.
151	
152	## Limits and caps
153	
154	Memory and output size do not depend on what a transcript contains.
155	
156	| Bound | Value | Behavior past it |
157	|---|---|---|
158	| Line length (`MaxLineBytes`) | 4 MiB | line skipped, counted in `OversizedLines`, never held in memory |
159	| `FileIssue` entries per file | 100, for `IssueUnreadable` and `IssueOversized` only | counters keep counting, entries stop. `IssueOpenFailed` and `IssueReadError` occur once per file and are always kept |
160	| Lines without id in the table | 100000, for the whole session (all files together) | still counted in tokens, `Messages` and `NoMessageID`, but aggregated without a table entry |
161	| Models per agent / versions per session | 64 | extra ones dropped |
162	| Label length | 128 bytes | truncated |
163	| Meta file | 1 MiB | refused (`MetaUnreadable`) |
164	| Sessions listed (`ListSessions`) | 10000 | the oldest are dropped and counted in `Listing.Omitted` |
165	| `cwd` probe (`ListSessions`) | first 8 MiB of each kept transcript | `Project` is `""` |
166	| `Session.Project` length | 4096 bytes | truncated |
167	
168	The 10000 cap applies after the directories are read: there is **no bound on
169	memory or time before it**. Every entry of every project directory is read and
170	stat-ed first, so a very large projects tree costs that much before the cap
171	trims the result. Only the `cwd` probe, run on the kept sessions, is bounded.
172	
173	## Known risk: a FIFO swapped in between `Lstat` and `Open`
174	
175	`openPlain` (`safeopen.go`) calls `Lstat`, refuses links and non-regular
176	files, opens the file, then compares the handle with the `Lstat` result using
177	`os.SameFile`. That closes the check-then-open window for links. It does not
178	for a regular file replaced by a **FIFO** between `Lstat` and `Open`: `os.Open`
179	blocks until a writer appears, before `SameFile` can run. Closing it would need
180	`O_NONBLOCK`, which the `os` package does not offer portably. The window is tiny
181	and the attacker must already control the transcripts directory. Accepted and
182	documented in the code. `ListSessions` has the same exposure: it opens each
183	kept transcript through `openPlain` to read its `cwd`, so a FIFO swapped in
184	there can block the listing (and so the view's read, which runs in a `Cmd`).
185	Carried over unchanged, not closed.
186	
187	## Diagnostics and `Degraded`
188	
189	`Diagnostics.Degraded()` is true if anything was skipped or guessed: unreadable
190	or oversized lines, `NoUsage`, `NoMessageID`, `CrossFileDuplicates`, meta
191	missing or unreadable, truncated files, or any `FileIssue`. A consumer should
192	show the totals as usual and flag them as approximate when it is true. A new
193	counter must be added to `Degraded()`.
194	
195	## Verification
196	
197	- **Spike S-01**: the parsing rules were checked against ccusage on 3 real
198	  sessions, with a **0.00 %** difference.
199	- **Fixtures** in `internal/agentusage/testdata/` are synthetic: shape follows
200	  Claude Code 2.1.302, every value is invented. `v2.1.302-basic/`,
201	  `synthetic-other-version/` (renamed or absent usage, unknown line type) and
202	  `damaged/` (bad line, file cut mid-JSON). Expected totals are written by hand
203	  in `parse_test.go`. See `testdata/README.md`.
204	- **Cross-check against ccusage** (step 6 of S-02, DEVDESK-54), reference
205	  version `ccusage@20.0.43`. `crosscheck_test.go` compares `ParseSession` with
206	  a reference file and is **skipped unless `DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF` is set**
207	  (path of the reference file). CI never sets it, so **CI does not run this
208	  test**: run it by hand. `DEVDESK_CLAUDE_PROJECTS` points to the projects
209	  directory to read (default: `ProjectsRoot()`). Each session is looked up as
210	  `<root>/<project>/<id>.jsonl`.
211	  The reference file is produced by the `mise` task:
212	
213	  ```bash
214	  mise run agentusage-ref -- <uuid>... > /path/outside/repo/ref.json
215	  DEVDESK_CCUSAGE_REF=/path/outside/repo/ref.json go test ./internal/agentusage -run TestSessionTotalsMatchCcusage -v
216	  ```
217	
218	  The task needs a POSIX shell, `npx` and `jq` (no Windows), and runs with
219	  `set -euo pipefail`: a failing ccusage call fails the task. For each session
220	  id it runs `ccusage claude session --id <uuid> --json` and writes
221	  `{"sessions": [{id, total, input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, ...]}`,
222	  where `total` is ccusage's `totalTokens` and the four others are sums over its
223	  `entries`. Write the file **outside the repository**: it comes from real
224	  sessions and must never be committed.
225	
226	  Only `total` is required. `input`, `output`, `cacheRead` and `cacheWrite` are
227	  optional per session: when present, each is compared too, and each must be
228	  within the tolerance (2 %, strictly below). A session whose transcript is not
229	  found, or whose parsing fails, fails the test.

231	## The `:agent-usage` view
232	
233	`internal/ui/agentusageview`, opened with `:agent-usage` or `:au`. It lists the
234	Claude Code sessions found on this machine, newest first, and reads only where
235	and when a session ran at this level (see the privacy amendment above). `→` or
236	`enter` opens the selected session's agents (DEVDESK-42, below).
237	
238	| Column | Content |
239	|---|---|
240	| Project | the `cwd`, **full path** with home folded to `~` (`theme.FoldHome`, done once per row in `Update`, never in a `Cell`). Cut from the left when too narrow, so the leaf stays visible. `-` (dim) when the transcript named none. |
241	| Last active | the transcript's `ModTime`, local time, `2006-01-02 15:04` |
242	| Session | the first 8 characters of the ID. `Optional`: the first column dropped on a narrow terminal. The filter (`/`) matches the full ID. |
243	
244	- **Rule 139.** The body is always `m.table.View()`. Loading, an empty
245	  machine and a filter with no match all leave a table with its header.
246	- **Header** (`GetHeaderInfo`): `Sessions` (rows visible after the filter) and,
247	  only when non-zero, `Skipped` (`Listing.Omitted`).
248	- **Footer** (Rule 128), derived on every frame with no timer, in this order:
249	  a failed read (red, "Failed to list Claude Code sessions — check logs"; the
250	  error is logged, never shown, since it can name a path), then loading (spinner,
251	  "Reading Claude Code sessions..."), then "No Claude Code sessions found in
252	  <root>" when the listing is empty before any filter.
253	- **Shortcuts**: `ctrl+r` Refresh, `/` Filter, `?` Help. The same keys in every
254	  state, none greyed (Rule 130): each always acts. `.` cycles the sort column
255	  and is listed in `?` only (Rule 138).
256	- **Reload on every entry.** The view is built once and stays cached in the
257	  router (`createView` stops if it already exists). The reload comes from
258	  `switchView` (`internal/app/command_line.go`), which calls `Init()` on every
259	  entry, and `Init` starts a read. The rows from the previous visit stay on
260	  screen until the answer arrives. Unlike `ctrl+r`, this entry reload shows no
261	  spinner and no "Reading..." line, because `Init` cannot set `loading` to
262	  true. `ctrl+r` reads again under a new generation number, and a stale answer
263	  (older generation) is dropped. A failed refresh keeps the previous rows: they
264	  are dated, not wrong.
265	- **Rule 110.** `listSessionsCmd` resolves `ProjectsRoot()` and calls
266	  `ListSessions` inside the `Cmd` and returns a message; `Update` alone touches
267	  the model.
268	
269	### Second level: the session's agents (DEVDESK-42)
270	
271	`→`/`enter` on a session opens its agents; `←`/`esc` goes back to the list.
272	`agents.go` builds the table, `availability.go` decides what the keys allow.
273	
274	| Column | Content |
275	|---|---|
276	| Agent | `orchestrator`, then each sub-agent's type behind `├─ ` / `└─ ` (`unknown` when the meta file gave none). `/` also matches the agent ID, which no column shows. |
277	| Model | the models the agent used, comma-separated; `-` (dim) when none |
278	| In, Out, Cache read, Cache write, Total | token counts. `Cache write` is the first column dropped on a narrow terminal, then `Cache read`. |
279	
280	- **Compact tokens.** `formatTokens` floors to one decimal (`1099` is `1.0k`,
281	  never `1.1k`) and drops the decimal from 100 of a unit up. Units: `k M B T`.
282	  Zeros are dim (Rule 122).
283	- **`≥` on Out.** A sub-agent whose output is partial (`Agent.PartialOutput()`,
284	  transcript still being written) shows `≥ ` before its Out count: a floor, not
285	  an exact value. The orchestrator never does.
286	- **Flat tree, two levels.** Whatever `SpawnDepth` a sub-agent has, it is a
287	  direct child of the orchestrator in the table. Order: orchestrator first, then
288	  sub-agents sorted by ID (stable). No column sorts, and `.` is greyed out.
289	- **Breadcrumb.** `Sessions › <project> › <short ID>` sits in the footer, one row
290	  above the filter bar and the message line (Rule 123), and adds one row to
291	  `GetFooterHeight`.
292	- **Header**: `Agents` and `Tokens` (sum of Total), both following the filter.
293	- **Footer status**: a failed read (red, "Failed to read this session — check
294	  logs"), then loading (spinner, "Reading session..."), then, when
295	  `Diagnostics.Degraded()`, a warning "Totals are approximate — some transcript
296	  data could not be read".
297	- **Availability (Rule 130).** The shortcut keys are identical at both levels;
298	  only `Disabled` changes, computed once in `availability()` and read by
299	  `GetShortcuts` and by the handlers through `guard`, which refuses with a Warn
300	  carrying the reason. `→` is greyed with no session selected or already inside
301	  a session; `esc` at the session list; `.` at the agents level.
302	- **Rule 110.** `parseSessionCmd` calls `ParseSession` inside a `Cmd`. Each parse
303	  carries `agentGen`, bumped on open, on `ctrl+r` and on leaving the level; an
304	  answer with another generation, or arriving after the user went back, is
305	  dropped. `ctrl+r` at the agents level re-parses the open session.
306	
307	**Privacy.** The view displays the project directory, the date, the session ID,
308	agent types, models and token counts. It never displays or logs the paths of
309	files a session touched, nor any content (prompt, reply, tool input or output):
310	`Usage` holds numbers and labels only, as stated in "Privacy" above.
311	
312	Known limits: the FIFO risk and the lack of a memory or time bound before the
313	10000-session cap (see "Limits and caps") both apply to this view's read. Claude
314	Code deletes old transcripts itself (30 days by default), so older sessions
315	disappear from the list.

6	## Criterion 1: does ccusage give tokens per sub-agent?
7	
8	Three finished sessions with `subagents/`, all on 2.1.302. "Own" = sum over parent + `subagents/agent-*.jsonl`, keeping the **last** line per `message.id` (map shared by the whole session), with `<synthetic>` excluded. Totals = in + out + cache-read + cache-write.
9	
10	| Session | Sub-agents | Msgs | Per sub-agent? | ccusage total | Own total | Δ own vs ccusage | `cost-state` total | Δ own vs cost-state (total / output) |
11	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
12	| d9acf4b8 (small) | 4 | 77 | **No** | 5,690,886 | 5,690,886 | 0.00 % | 7,060,896 | −19.4 % / −66.7 % |
13	| 8bc69d30 (medium) | 14 | 143 | **No** | 15,659,603 | 15,659,603 | 0.00 % | 20,048,361 | −21.9 % / −58.7 % |
14	| aa37ed75 (large) | 32 | 631 | **No** | 68,172,620 | 68,172,620 | 0.00 % | 84,286,088 | −19.1 % / −66.1 % |
15	
16	- **The gap is confirmed.** ccusage returns one row per session, plus a per-model breakdown with `--breakdown`. Its JSON `entries` carry no agent id. `--by-agent` on the top-level `session` command means *per CLI* (every row is `agent: "claude"`), not per sub-agent. ccusage does read the sub-agent files and counts them in the session total: its entry count equals the number of `message.id`s.
17	- **Dedup.** ccusage matches last-line dedup on every field (0.00 %). Keeping the first line instead loses 0 %, −3.3 % and −23.6 % of `output_tokens`. A naive sum inflates the total ×1.52 / ×1.80 / ×1.95.
18	- **Reference for the 2 % rule: ccusage**, at the session level (it has no per-agent figure to compare against). `cost-state` cannot be the reference:
19	  - it is 19 to 22 % above the transcripts, structurally;
20	  - it is per model, not per agent;
21	  - it is only written when the session closes (34 of 36 files have it only in their last 5 lines; it is missing from the live session).
22	- **Root cause (new, affects S-02/S-07).** On sub-agent messages, the last line per `message.id` has `stop_reason: null` (94 % on 2.1.302, 80 % on 2.1.283), and its `output_tokens` is a streaming placeholder (median 8 tokens).
23	  - The completion notification's `totalTokens` minus the last message's context gives a real output of several hundred tokens for that last message. Sub-agent **output is therefore a lower bound**, in ccusage too.
24	  - `cache_read` is also 24 to 32 % higher in `cost-state`, with no matching `api-request` line (79 requests for 77 messages): those API calls are not in the transcripts.
25	  - Cache-write agrees within 0.7 to 3.2 %. Input tokens differ a lot in relative terms but are negligible in absolute terms. Output weighs ≤ 0.3 % of total tokens, so **ranking agents by tokens is unaffected**; cost per agent is.
26	- A per-agent signal exists in the parent (`attachment.queued_command.usage {totalTokens, toolUses, durationMs}`). But it is linked to its agent only through the notification text (content), and `totalTokens` is the final context size, not a cumulative total. **Not usable.**

3	import (
4		"bufio"
5		"bytes"
6		"errors"
7		"io"
8	)
9	
10	// readerBufferBytes is the bufio buffer size; longer lines are reassembled.
11	const readerBufferBytes = 64 << 10
12	
13	// MaxLineBytes is the longest line (newline excluded) kept in memory.
14	const MaxLineBytes = 4 << 20
15	
16	// scanResult describes what scanLines consumed.
17	type scanResult struct {
18		// Consumed is the offset just past the last complete line.
19		Consumed int64
20		// Oversized counts complete lines longer than maxLen that were skipped.
21		Oversized int
22		// OversizedAt holds the offset of each skipped line, in order.
23		OversizedAt []int64
24		// Tail holds the bytes after the last newline (an incomplete line).
25		Tail []byte
26	}
27	
28	// scanLines calls fn for every complete, non-empty line of r no longer
29	// than maxLen bytes. off is the offset of the line's first byte; line has no
30	// trailing "\n" or "\r" and is only valid during the call: fn must copy it
31	// to keep it. Complete lines longer than maxLen are skipped without being held
32	// in memory. An incomplete final line is returned in Tail whatever its
33	// length, unless it already exceeds maxLen: it is then dropped, and counted in
34	// neither Consumed nor Oversized (it may never be completed). A Tail of
35	// maxLen+1 or maxLen+2 bytes is still kept (the cutoff is maxLen+2, since a
36	// "\r" may follow); one longer than that is dropped.
37	func scanLines(r io.Reader, maxLen int, fn func(line []byte, off int64)) (scanResult, error) {
38		br := bufio.NewReaderSize(r, readerBufferBytes)
39		var (
40			res      scanResult
41			pending  []byte // line prefix reassembled across buffer fills
42			skipping bool   // the current line is already known to be too long
43			pos      int64  // bytes read so far
44		)
45		start := int64(0) // offset of the current line's first byte
46		for {
47			chunk, err := br.ReadSlice('\n')
48			pos += int64(len(chunk))
49			if !skipping {
50				// maxLen+1 bytes are kept so a trailing "\r" does not count against maxLen.
51				if len(pending)+len(chunk) > maxLen+2 { // +1 more: chunk may end with "\n"
52					skipping, pending = true, nil
53				} else {
54					pending = append(pending, chunk...)
55				}
56			}
57			switch {
58			case err == nil:
59				if skipping {
60					res.skip(start)
61				} else {
62					res.emit(pending, start, maxLen, fn)
63				}
64				res.Consumed = pos
65				start, pending, skipping = pos, pending[:0], false
66			case errors.Is(err, bufio.ErrBufferFull):
67			case errors.Is(err, io.EOF):
68				if !skipping {
69					res.Tail = bytes.Clone(pending)
70				}
71				return res, nil
72			default:
73				return res, err
74			}
75		}
76	}
77	
78	// emit trims the line terminator from raw (which ends with "\n") and hands
79	// the line to fn, or counts it as oversized.
80	func (res *scanResult) emit(raw []byte, off int64, maxLen int, fn func([]byte, int64)) {
81		line := bytes.TrimSuffix(bytes.TrimSuffix(raw, []byte("\n")), []byte("\r"))
82		switch {
83		case len(line) > maxLen:
84			res.skip(off)
85		case len(line) > 0:
86			fn(line, off)
87		}
88	}
89	
90	// skip counts one oversized line starting at off.
91	func (res *scanResult) skip(off int64) {
92		res.Oversized++
93		res.OversizedAt = append(res.OversizedAt, off)
94	}

8	
9	// Bounds that keep memory and output size independent of what a transcript
10	// contains.
11	const (
12		// maxFileIssuesPerFile caps the unreadable/oversized FileIssue entries
13		// kept per file; the counters keep counting past it.
14		maxFileIssuesPerFile = 100
15		// maxNoIDEntries caps the per-message table for lines without a message
16		// id. Past it a line still counts in NoMessageID, Messages and tokens,
17		// but gets no table entry.
18		maxNoIDEntries    = 100000
19		maxModelsPerAgent = 64
20		maxVersions       = 64
21		// maxLabelLen is the longest label (model, version, id, file name) kept, in bytes.
22		maxLabelLen = 128
23	)
24	
25	// sanitizeLabel cleans a short label read from disk; see sanitize.
26	func sanitizeLabel(s string) string { return sanitize(s, maxLabelLen) }
27	
28	// sanitize replaces with '?' every invalid UTF-8 byte, every control character
29	// (C0, DEL and C1, so a raw or encoded 0x9B CSI included) and every format
30	// character (category Cf: bidi overrides and isolates, zero-width marks), then
31	// truncates the result to maxLen bytes, without splitting a UTF-8 sequence
32	// when it can be avoided. Text read from disk reaches a terminal, where an
33	// escape sequence would be interpreted and a bidi override would reorder it.
34	func sanitize(s string, maxLen int) string {
35		if len(s) > maxLen {
36			cut := maxLen
37			for cut > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(s[cut]) {
38				cut--
39			}
40			s = s[:cut]
41		}
42		var b strings.Builder
43		for _, r := range s { // an invalid byte ranges as utf8.RuneError
44			if r == utf8.RuneError || unicode.IsControl(r) || unicode.Is(unicode.Cf, r) {
45				r = '?'
46			}
47			b.WriteRune(r)
48		}
49		return b.String()
50	}
51	
52	// modelSet is an insertion-ordered set of at most maxModelsPerAgent models.
53	type modelSet struct {
54		list []string
55		seen map[string]bool
56	}
57	
58	// add keeps model unless it is empty, already listed, or the set is full.
59	func (s *modelSet) add(model string) {
60		if model == "" || len(s.list) >= maxModelsPerAgent || s.seen[model] {
61			return
62		}
63		if s.seen == nil {
64			s.seen = map[string]bool{}
65		}
66		s.seen[model] = true
67		s.list = append(s.list, model)
68	}

6	)
7	
8	// errNotPlain is returned when a path is not what Lstat said it was a moment
9	// ago (swapped for a link or another file). It is fixed so it never carries
10	// a path or content.
11	var errNotPlain = errors.New("agentusage: path changed while being opened")
12	
13	// errNotRegular is returned when a path is a symbolic link or not a regular
14	// file as seen by Lstat.
15	var errNotRegular = errors.New("agentusage: not a regular file")
16	
17	// openPlain opens path only if it is not a symbolic link and its mode, as
18	// reported by Lstat, matches wantDir. The opened handle is compared with the
19	// Lstat result (os.SameFile), which closes the window between checking and
20	// opening. On Windows the file identity is read lazily, at the SameFile call.
21	// A missing path yields an error satisfying os.ErrNotExist; a path of the
22	// wrong kind yields (nil, nil).
23	//
24	// Known limit, accepted: a regular file swapped for a FIFO between Lstat and
25	// Open makes os.Open block until a writer appears, before the SameFile check
26	// can run. Closing it would need O_NONBLOCK, which the os package does not
27	// offer portably. The window is tiny and the attacker must already control
28	// the transcripts directory.
29	func openPlain(path string, wantDir bool) (*os.File, error) {
30		li, err := os.Lstat(path)
31		if err != nil {
32			return nil, err
33		}
34		if li.IsDir() != wantDir || (!wantDir && !li.Mode().IsRegular()) {
35			return nil, nil
36		}
37		f, err := os.Open(path)
38		if err != nil {
39			return nil, err
40		}
41		fi, err := f.Stat()
42		if err != nil || !os.SameFile(li, fi) {
43			_ = f.Close()
44			if err == nil {
45				err = errNotPlain
46			}
47			return nil, err
48		}
49		return f, nil
50	}

32	// tools and descriptions are deliberately not declared, so encoding/json
33	// skips them without keeping them. The root "type" key is not consulted.

35		Version json.RawMessage `json:"version"`
36		Message *wireMessage    `json:"message"`
37	}

41		Model      json.RawMessage `json:"model"`
42		StopReason json.RawMessage `json:"stop_reason"`

44	}

47	// value can be told apart from an absent one.
48	type wireUsage struct {

50		Output     json.RawMessage `json:"output_tokens"`

53	}

55	// decodeLine extracts the usage fields of one transcript line. A message
56	// without usage counts as kindNoUsage only if it has an id or a model (an
57	// assistant turn whose usage went missing or was renamed). It never
58	// reports a decoder error: those can quote line content, so a bad line is
59	// just kindUnreadable.
60	func decodeLine(b []byte) (record, lineKind) {
61		var w wireLine
62		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &w); err != nil {
63			return record{}, kindUnreadable
64		}
65		m := w.Message
66		if m == nil {
67			return record{Version: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version))}, kindIgnored
68		}
69		rec := record{
70			MessageID: m.ID,
71			Model:     sanitizeLabel(optString(m.Model)),
72			Version:   sanitizeLabel(optString(w.Version)),
73			StopNull:  isNullOrAbsent(m.StopReason),
74		}
75		switch {

77			return rec, kindSynthetic

79			// User and tool-result lines carry a message without id, usage or model.
80			return rec, kindIgnored
81		case m.Usage == nil:
82			return rec, kindNoUsage
83		}

86			return record{}, kindUnreadable
87		}

93	// non-negative integer.

95		var t Tokens
96		for _, c := range []struct {
97			raw json.RawMessage
98			dst *int64
99		}{{u.Input, &t.Input}, {u.Output, &t.Output}, {u.CacheRead, &t.CacheRead}, {u.CacheWrite, &t.CacheWrite}} {
100			n, ok := parseCounter(c.raw)
101			if !ok {
102				return Tokens{}, false
103			}
104			*c.dst = n
105		}
106		return t, true
107	}

110	func parseCounter(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
111		if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
112			return 0, true
113		}
114		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(string(raw), 10, 64)
115		return n, err == nil && n >= 0
116	}

119	// of another type: metadata of an unexpected type must not cost the line.
120	func optString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
121		var s string
122		if len(raw) == 0 || raw[0] != '"' || json.Unmarshal(raw, &s) != nil {
123			return ""
124		}
125		return s
126	}

129	// other value, whatever its type, counts as a stop reason being set.
130	func isNullOrAbsent(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
131		return len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null"
132	}

33	}

36	const maxMetaBytes = 1 << 20
37

39	var (
40		errMalformedMeta = errors.New("agentusage: malformed meta file")
41		errMetaTooBig    = errors.New("agentusage: meta file too large")
42		errMetaNotPlain  = errors.New("agentusage: meta file is not a regular file")
43	)

45	// readMeta reads a meta file. A missing file yields an error satisfying
46	// errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist). A symbolic link or non-regular file is
47	// refused, and reading is bounded by maxMetaBytes.
48	func readMeta(path string) (meta, error) {
49		f, err := openPlain(path, false)
50		if err != nil {
51			return meta{}, err
52		}
53		if f == nil {
54			return meta{}, errMetaNotPlain
55		}
56		defer func() { _ = f.Close() }()
57		b, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, maxMetaBytes+1))
58		if err != nil {
59			return meta{}, err
60		}
61		if len(b) > maxMetaBytes {
62			return meta{}, errMetaTooBig
63		}
64		var w wireMeta
65		if json.Unmarshal(b, &w) != nil {
66			return meta{}, errMalformedMeta
67		}
68		m := meta{AgentType: sanitizeLabel(optString(w.AgentType))}
69		var fin bool
70		if json.Unmarshal(w.Finished, &fin) == nil && string(w.Finished) != "null" {
71			m.Finished = &fin // absent, null or a wrong type: stays nil
72		}
73		if len(w.SpawnDepth) > 0 {
74			_ = json.Unmarshal(w.SpawnDepth, &m.SpawnDepth) // wrong type: stays 0
75			m.SpawnDepth = max(m.SpawnDepth, 0)
76		}
77		return m, nil
78	}
79	
80	// state maps the finished flag; absent or null is StateUnknown.
81	func (m meta) state() State {
82		switch {
83		case m.Finished == nil:
84			return StateUnknown
85		case *m.Finished:
86			return StateFinished
87		}
88		return StateUnfinished
89	}

1	# Agent usage S-04: spot the most expensive agent (DEVDESK-43)
2	
3	Story: at the agents level of `:agent-usage`, sorting by tokens puts the
4	largest agent first (total = in + out + cache read + cache write; a partial
5	sub-agent output changes nothing in the ranking). Each agent shows its share
6	of the session total in %, the shares add up to 100 % with the rounding
7	residue absorbed by the orchestrator row; a partial sub-agent's Out keeps its
8	`≥`. Two agents of the same `agentType` stay distinct (short agent ID). The
9	sort uses `.` (Rule 111). Out of scope: live (S-05b), cost (S-07), state /
10	duration (S-06), nested tree by `toolUseId`.
11	
12	## What exists today (checked on `main` @ df35c82)
13	
14	- `internal/ui/agentusageview/agents.go`: `agentRow{Agent, last bool}`,
15	  `agentRows(u)` (orchestrator, then sub-agents by ID), `agentColumns()`:
16	  `Agent | Model | In | Out | Cache read | Cache write | Total`, **no `Less`**.
17	  `roleCell` prefixes `├─ ` / `└─ ` from `last`. `formatTokens` floors.
18	  `agentSearch` matches role + full agent ID (no column shows the ID).
19	- `model.go`: `agentTable` built with `SortColumn: -1`, reused across sessions
20	  (`openSelected` clears its filter and items, not its sort).
21	- `availability.go`: `actions.Sort` is unavailable at the agents level
22	  (`reasonAgentsUnsorted`); `update.go` refuses `.` there with a `Warn`.
23	  `GetShortcuts` has five keys (`ctrl+r → esc / ?`); `.` is in `?` only.
24	- `internal/ui/datatable`: `Column.Less`, `Config.SortColumn/SortDesc`,
25	  `CycleSort` (asc → desc → next column; back to unsorted when the table
26	  opened unsorted), `SortState`, `SetSort`, header arrow ` ▲`/` ▼`, `askFor`
27	  reserves `len(Title)+2` for a sortable column. `sort.SliceStable`, so ties
28	  keep input order (orchestrator first, then by ID).
29	- Drop order on a narrow terminal (`widths.go` `drop`): rightmost
30	  `Optional+DropFirst`, then rightmost `Optional`, then rightmost of the rest.
31	- Real sub-agent IDs on this machine: 172 of 172 are `a` + 16 hex (17 chars),

36	## Questions bloquantes
37	
38	**Q1. What does the agents table show on open, and what does `.` do?**
39	Criterion 1 says "when I sort by tokens, the largest is first", not how many
40	presses away that is. Today `CycleSort` goes ascending first, which puts the
41	*smallest* agent on top.
42	- **A (recommended)**: opens as the tree (DEVDESK-42 unchanged). Only `Total`
43	  is sortable. `.` cycles **tree → Total ▼ (largest first) → Total ▲ → tree**.
44	  Needs one additive field in `datatable`, `Column.DescFirst` (step 1): the
45	  first press on such a column sorts descending. No other table changes
46	  behaviour.
47	- B: opens sorted by Total ▼; `.` cycles Total ▲ → tree → Total ▼. Largest
48	  agent visible with no key (brief: "identified in < 5 s"), but the tree is no
49	  longer the first thing seen, and `CycleSort` cannot reach "unsorted" from a
50	  table that opened sorted: needs a second datatable change
51	  (`Config.UnsortedStop bool` or similar). +1 S.
52	- C: every count column sortable (In, Out, Cache read, Cache write, Total),
53	  each descending first. 11 states on the cycle; Total ▼ is the 9th press.
54	
55	**Q2. How is a share written?** It sets the column width and every expected
56	string.
57	- **A (recommended)**: one decimal, **floored**, `12.3%`, `100.0%`, `0.0%`
58	  (width 6). Each sub-agent is floored to the tenth; the orchestrator gets
59	  `100.0 − Σ sub-agents`, so the sum is exactly `100.0%` and no row is ever
60	  shown above what it counted (same floor rule as `formatTokens`).
61	- B: integer percent, floored, same absorption: `12%` (width 5, the title).
62	  Narrower, but most sub-agents of a large session read `0%`.
63	- C: rounded to nearest (A or B precision). Closer per row, but the
64	  orchestrator's residue can go negative on a session of many small agents
65	  and would have to be clamped, breaking the 100 %.
66	
67	**Q3. Which columns give way on a narrow terminal?** Adding `ID` (8) and
68	`Share` (6) and the sort arrow on Total costs 18 cells. With today's flags,
69	at 60 columns `Total` and `Share` themselves would be dropped (rightmost
70	non-optional first), which defeats the story.
71	- **A (recommended)**: make `In` and `Model` `Optional` too. Drop order:
72	  Cache write → Cache read → In → Model. Computed from `availableFor`:
73	  100 cols: all but Cache write; **80 cols: Agent, ID, Model, In, Out, Total,
74	  Share** (Cache read is lost at 80, it was kept by DEVDESK-42); 60 cols:
75	  Agent, ID, Out, Total, Share; 50 cols: Share goes too.
76	- B: keep Cache read at 80 by making `Model` go before it (Model
77	  `Optional+DropFirst` alongside Cache write). 80 cols: Agent, ID, In, Out,
78	  Cache read, Total, Share. Loses the model name, which tells a sub-agent on
79	  Haiku from one on Opus.
80	- C: no ID column; the ID goes into the Agent cell (`├─ coder a0044dcf`).
81	  Saves the 2 padding cells only, and the ID is what truncation cuts first
82	  in a `SizingContent` column, so criterion 3 fails on a narrow terminal.
83	
84	The plan assumes **A / A / A**. Q1 B adds a datatable sub-step to step 1 and
85	changes step 4's cycle tests; Q2 B changes `formatShare` and the Share width
86	only; Q3 B changes two flags in step 3 and its width tests.

88	## Assumptions (reversible, no impact outside this story)
89	
90	- H1. **Sorted means flat.** While a sort is active, no row carries `├─ `/`└─ `:
91	  the orchestrator may sit mid-list and a `└─` there would lie. The row says
92	  `orchestrator` or the sub-agent type, and the ID column tells them apart. The
93	  branch is precomputed per row (`agentRow.branch`), since a `Cell` cannot see
94	  the sort state: on every `.` at the agents level, the view rebuilds the rows
95	  with `agentRows(u, tree)` and calls `Remeasure()` (a user action, Agent
96	  narrows by 3 cells).
97	- H2. **Share is of the whole session**, not of the filtered rows: a filter
98	  `coder` still shows coder's 12.3 %. The header `Tokens` keeps following the
99	  filter (DEVDESK-42). Total for shares = `u.Total().Total()`.
100	- H3. **No `≥` on Share.** Criterion 2 asks it on Out only. A partial
101	  sub-agent's share is computed on its (floor) total like any other.
102	- H4. **Short ID**: one length for the whole session, the smallest `n ≥ 8`
103	  (runes) for which every sub-agent ID prefix is distinct, capped at the full
104	  ID. An ID shorter than `n` shows whole. Two identical IDs (cannot come from
105	  `LocateSession`, file names are unique) show whole and stay identical. The
106	  orchestrator's ID cell is `-` (dim).
107	- H5. **ID column**: right after Agent, `SizingContent`, `MinWidth 8`, never
108	  dropped (criterion 3), `Search` = full ID. The ID leaves `agentSearch`
109	  (moved, not duplicated): `/` matches it exactly as before.
110	- H6. **Share column**: last, `SizingFixed`, width 6, no `Less` (same order
111	  as Total), dim when the share is `0` or `-`. A session with zero tokens
112	  shows `-` on every row, no 100 % claim.
113	- H7. **`.` in the header**, at both levels: `{Key: ".", Description: "Sort"}`,
114	  never greyed (both levels now sort). `jobsview`, `security`, `netdiag`,
115	  `oci_resources` all announce it; DEVDESK-41 kept it in `?` only because the
116	  agents level could not sort. `Sort` and `reasonAgentsUnsorted` leave
117	  `availability.go`. If refused, revert to five keys, no other step changes.
118	- H8. **The sort survives** `esc` + opening another session, and `ctrl+r`
119	  (the table is reused, the choice is not session-specific, unlike the filter
120	  that `openSelected` already clears). The cursor is not moved by a sort
121	  (datatable behaviour everywhere); it starts on row 0 after an open, so the
122	  largest agent is the selected one after `.`.
123	- H9. **The residue goes to the `Main` agent.** If a `Usage` has none (not
124	  produced by `ParseSession`), every share is floored and the sum may read
125	  below 100 %. Saturated totals (`math.MaxInt64`) are clamped: the residue is
126	  never negative, the sum may then exceed 100 %; the session is absurd and
127	  stated as such in the doc, not handled further.
128	- H10. `DescFirst` is a `datatable` change because Rule 101 wants `.` to
129	  behave the same everywhere: declaring "descending first" on the column is
130	  the same reasoning `Config.SortDesc` already documents for count columns.
131	  The alternative, a view-local cycle over `SetSort`, would be a second
132	  implementation of `.`.
